rationale: The base station lost its internet uplink after the customer's router was replaced, showing solid red LED, E-503, and all devices offline in the app while the base station remained reachable locally (some sensors still responded). A proper ordered power-cycle (router first, then base station) restored the uplink — the customer confirmed the LED turned solid blue and all devices came back online. This is a frontline-resolvable network/uplink issue, not a hardware fault.

repair_steps: Power-cycle the router: unplug power, wait 30 seconds, plug back in, wait until internet light is stable.
Power-cycle the base station: unplug power, wait 10 seconds, plug back in.
Wait 2-3 minutes and confirm the base station LED turns solid blue and all devices show online in the app.

A proper restart of both devices has restored the connection. Your system should now be fully operational. If you notice any further issues, please don't hesitate to reach out.

args.action: Check the Ethernet cable going into the base station. Make sure it is plugged into one of the LAN ports on the new router (not the WAN/Internet port), and that the other end is firmly seated in the base station's Ethernet port. If it was on Wi-Fi instead, the new router has a different Wi-Fi name/password, so the base station can't reconnect — in that case connect it with an Ethernet cable to a LAN port. Then power-cycle the base station (unplug power, wait 10 seconds, plug back in) and wait 2 minutes. Report the LED color afterward.

args.question: Can you look at the back of the new router and tell me which port the base station's cable is plugged into? Routers usually have one port labeled WAN/Internet (often a different color or separated from the others) and several LAN ports. Also, is there any Ethernet cable plugged into the base station at all, or does it only have the power cable?

args.action: On the new router, unplug the base station's Ethernet cable and plug it into a different port (try each of the LAN ports one at a time). After each change, wait about 30 seconds and check the base station LED. Also confirm the router itself has internet by checking that your laptop's Wi-Fi still loads a website. If the LED turns solid blue on any port, stop there and report which port worked.
